items.title: Sword-wielding man leaves two injured in Gua Musang
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: Two men were injured after being slashed with a sword during a fight at a rubber store at Rancangan Pemulihan Tanah (RPT) Kesedar Sungai Terah yesterday. Gua Musang police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred during a discussion where a 27-year-old man allegedly tried to pull out a sword tucked behind his back. The suspect then swung the sword.

items.title: Hong Kong arrests 9 over fuel smuggling as oil prices surge
items.summary: HONG KONG: Hong Kong arrested nine people in a city-wide operation targeting illicit fuel activities, authorities said on Wednesday, as surging global oil prices continue to put pressure on the import-dependent financial hub. Prices at Hong Kong's filling stations are among the world's most expensive, creating a growing incentive for smugglers to transport cheaper fuel illegally across the border into the city. Authorities said they seized more than 30,000 litres of smuggled fuel worth more than HK$1 million (US$127,000) in September, arresting eight men and one woman.

items.title: Singapore set to miss 2035 green-power import target
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore is set to fall short of its 2035 target of importing 6 gigawatts of low-carbon electricity, a report from research and consultancy firm Wood Mackenzie said on Wednesday. The country has approved 9.25 GW of import capacity across six corridors, but none of the projects has reached financial close or begun construction, the report added. By 2035, imported green power is likely to be at 15 per cent of its power generation mix, roughly half of EMA's target of about one-third of projected demand at 6 GW.

items.title: 'We don't have a future': French students protest school conditions
items.summary: As drums pounded and chants rang out, 16-year-old Yanis, flanked by a knot of friends, rattled off why he had joined tens of thousands surging through the streets of Paris on Tuesday to demand better learning conditions. We can't study," the teenager from the northern Paris suburb of Sarcelles said, calling conditions at his high school "unacceptable". On Tuesday, protesters flooded into the Place de la Republique in central Paris, hoisting signs.

items.title: 713 deepfakes of political leaders taken offline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 713 image-manipulation and deepfake content involving political party leaders have been taken down between Jan 1, 2025 and Sept 15 this year. The Communications Ministry said the content was taken down following complaints, breaches of service providers' community guidelines and violations of local laws. "For content containing obscene, indecent, false, threatening, grossly offensive or harmful elements, MCMC may take action under the Communications and Multimedia Act or the Online Safety Act," it said in a written parliamentary reply today.

items.title: Mohamad: Early preparations underway for possible extreme El Nino heat
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The government is making early preparations for potentially extreme heat, with temperatures forecast to reach 40°C from the end of this year until April next year. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said his ministry is also seeking input from experts in artificial intelligence, science and technology to identify the best ways to deal with the expected weather changes. He said early preparations were important to ensure that the government and the people would not panic in the event of prolonged hot and dry weather.

items.title: Sri Lanka's Rajapaksa family hit as ex-first lady arrested in graft probe
items.summary: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka's anti-graft authority arrested former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa on Wednesday over allegations that her charity misused donations collected for a children's hospital, dealing a major blow to the once powerful family. President Anura Kumara Dissanayake's government has revived long-dormant graft investigations involving members of the once-powerful Rajapaksa family, which dominated Sri Lankan politics for nearly two decades. The 73-year-old wife of former president Mahinda was remanded in custody until Tuesday by a Colombo magistrate.

items.title: The arms race is becoming a debt race
items.summary: With the collective annual gross domestic product (GDP) now just over US$55 trillion for the US, Japan, Germany, France, Britain, Italy and Canada, an US$8 trillion increase over a decade amounts to almost 15 per cent of 2026's GDP. Across Europe alone, he said, broader defence goals imply roughly €4 trillion to €5 trillion of additional spending over the coming decade —rising towards €9 trillion "when adjacent infrastructure is included". The earmarked increase in US defence outlays in the 2027 fiscal year to a record US$1.5 trillion would surpass the World War 2 peak in inflation-adjusted dollars.

items.title: Thaksin fights US$504m tax claim, citing threat to personal safety
items.summary: BANGKOK: Ex-Thai premier Thaksin Shinawatra told a court on Wednesday that his life could be in danger if authorities seize assets including bullet-proof vehicles as part of a US$500 million, decades-old tax dispute. The Supreme Court's Tax Division last November upheld a tax claim by the Revenue Department against the former prime minister – one of Thailand's richest people – over the 2006 sale of his telecoms firm. Appearing at the Central Tax Court in Bangkok on Wednesday, Thaksin said those assets included five cars, two of them bullet-proof, which he linked to his personal safety.

items.title: NST Leader: Scam syndicates are evolving, Malaysia must outsmart them
items.summary: Receiving suspected scam calls is almost an everyday event for Malaysians now. Our crime-busters must, therefore, be quick to stay ahead of these syndicates as well. Scam operators are proving highly adaptable, mobile and increasingly technology-enabled.

items.title: Thailand, US trade deal down to final clause: PM
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Thailand is at "the last paragraph" of a trade agreement with the United States, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Wednesday. Speaking at a forum in Singapore, Anutin said he expected to sign the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade during President Donald Trump's next visit to Asia, likely in November in Manila or Shenzhen when Trump attends Asean meetings. Anutin said that he received a letter from Trump last week confirming the deal is at its final stage.

items.title: Govt reviewing SST for elderly care services
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Finance and Women, Family and Community Development Ministries are reviewing proposals to improve the Sales and Service Tax (SST) for elderly care services regulated by the Welfare Department. The Finance Ministry said the review would consider the type and nature of services provided, including basic and premium care, to ensure a more targeted tax treatment. "The government is aware of concerns over the impact of the service tax on the costs borne by elderly people receiving care services.

items.title: Nine states record 100pct Sara usage rate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nine states and federal territories to record a 100 per cent usage rate for the monthly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) as of Sept 20. "The lowest usage rates were recorded in Putrajaya at 94 per cent and Johor at 95 per cent. "This reflected a usage rate of 99.7 per cent, with transaction value in the local market reaching RM5.2 billion," the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply today.

items.title: Nurse, husband killed in motorcycle-lorry crash
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: A couple were killed in a motorcycle-lorry crash at Jalan Sungai Buloh, near the Sierramas exit today. Petaling Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police received a report on the crash at 3.50pm. "Preliminary investigations found that the crash occurred around 2.50pm.

items.title: Ex-cop, 76, has 12-year jail term, whipping upheld for assaulting girl, 5
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today upheld a retired policeman's 12-year prison sentence and two strokes of the rotan for sexually assaulting a five-year-old girl whom his daughter had been babysitting. A three-member bench comprising judges Datuk Azman Abdullah, K. Muniandy and Dean Wayne Daly dismissed the 76-year-old man's appeal against his conviction and sentence. Azman said there was overwhelming and convincing evidence, notwithstanding that the victim was eight years old when she gave evidence.

items.title: Fahmi: Finas to study residual payment mechanism for actors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Communications Ministry, through the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas), will study the residual payment or revenue-sharing mechanism for audiovisual works in Malaysia. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the study would take into account three main aspects, namely legislation, the structure of the creative industry ecosystem and current business models, and the practices of streaming platforms and international distributors. Fahmi said the Copyright Act 1987 currently provided certain rights to performers.

items.title: Ex-bank officer fined RM36,000 for bribery, now works as delivery rider
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A former bank officer was fined RM36,000 by the Sessions Court today on six charges of failing to report receiving more than RM80,000 in bribes for personal loan financing. Judge Rosli Ahmad imposed the sentence on Noor Iskandar Aziz, 45, and ordered him to serve six months' imprisonment if he failed to settle the fine. The gratification was for assisting the personal loan financing applications of customers of CSA Academy Sdn Bhd at a bank, concurrently with the personal loan applications of customers at several other financial institutions.

items.title: 2027 Budget to focus on growth, easing cost pressures, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The fifth Madani budget will focus on strengthening the economy while ensuring economic growth translates into better quality of life for the people, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said economic growth alone was insufficient if some people continued to face rising living costs. Earlier today, Anwar briefed the media on the 2027 Budget.

items.title: Toddler undergoes three surgeries after stray dog attack last month
items.summary: Nur Haira Wafiqah is currently warded at the Paediatric Special Surgery Ward of Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA), Johor Baru, where she is under the close supervision of seven specialist doctors, her father said. Mohammad Hamizi Hamdan, 37, said the first three surgeries involved treating and closing wounds on various parts of his daughter's body and head caused by the animal bites. "This is Haira's fourth week receiving treatment at HSA and she is scheduled to undergo another surgery on her head this week," he said.

items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. items.title: Indonesia records 1,201 hotspots as haze persists in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Forest and land fires in Indonesia continued to burn, with 1,201 high-confidence hotspots recorded nationwide today, down by 158 from yesterday. The Forestry Ministry said Central Kalimantan recorded 182 hotspots, the highest among the six priority provinces, followed by South Sumatra (71), West Kalimantan (34), Jambi (21) and South Kalimantan (18), while Riau recorded none. "For us at the Forestry Ministry, strengthening the forest police is very important to improve the monitoring and protection of forest areas, including from the threat of encroachment and forest fires," Raja Juli said in an Instagram post.

items.title: Malaysian Parliament's Palestine Caucus to submit motion on Gaza genocide for debate
items.summary: Its chairman, Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh, said the proposed motion would include calls for a lasting ceasefire, the protection of civilians, and safe, sustained and unhindered access to humanitarian aid. Syed Ibrahim, who is natural resources and environmental sustainability deputy minister, said this at a press conference held in conjunction with the Three-Year Commemoration of the Gaza Genocide at the Parliament building here today. The Ledang member of parliament also said the motion would call for efforts to strengthen diplomatic action, including scrutiny of military assistance and arms transfers that risk facilitating violations of international law.

items.title: Unsubsidised RON97 and RON95 up 15 sen, diesel holds at RM5.27
items.summary: The Finance Ministry (MoF) said the increase was driven by pressure on the supply of refined petroleum products in the international market, despite the gradual recovery of crude oil flows from West Asia. "Although crude oil flows from West Asia are gradually recovering, global crude oil prices remain high. The ministry said price pressures were increasingly concentrated on refined petroleum products following China's suspension of most fuel exports for October, limiting supplies in the international market.

items.title: Ketum stash found during social media livestream
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA: Police have confirmed the discovery of a container holding 21 bottles of liquid believed to be ketum juice at Kampung Seri Langkas, Puchong Permai, yesterday. Subang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said police received a report about the discovery at 8.45pm from a member of the public who live-streaming at the location. "An inspection of an unnumbered house found a covered plastic container holding 21 plastic bottles containing liquid believed to be ketum juice," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Nurse stabbed six times by husband in stable condition
items.summary: Her daughter, 19, said her mother regained consciousness yesterday afternoon but remained under close observation at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital (HRPZ II). "According to the doctors, my mother's condition started to stabilise today, but she still requires close monitoring by the hospital. She said her mother had also started speaking, although she remained weak.

items.title: Salutica eyes RM16.2m placement to fund property expansion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Salutica Bhd has proposed a private placement of up to 30 per cent of its issued shares to raise up to RM16.18 million to fund its expansion into property development and construction. Salutica said the proposed diversification would cover property development, construction and related activities. This includes design-and-build works, trading and supplying construction materials, property management and property investment.

items.title: Johor haze worsens as all monitoring stations record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Haze conditions worsened across Johor tonight, with all eight air quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. The state government and relevant agencies are continuing to monitor API readings as the haze situation develops. The worsening haze in Johor comes amid a wider regional haze situation, with neighbouring Indonesia also facing the effects of wildfires.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 7, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: Election timeline reasonable Caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the timeframe for the 16th Melaka election is reasonable, allowing adequate time for preparations and logistical arrangements. Fiscal deficit narrows Malaysia's fiscal deficit is projected to narrow to 3.3 per cent of GDP in 2027, keeping the government on track to meet its medium-term target of 3.0 per cent by 2028. Jealousy motive suspected Police believe jealousy was the motive behind the murder of a 19-year-old student, with the suspect allegedly confessing to strangling her after becoming upset over her meeting another man.

items.title: Pahang cops still hunting prime suspect in Genting jewellery heist
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pahang police are still hunting the suspected mastermind behind the RM1.7 million jewellery heist at SkyAvenue, Genting Highlands, following the arrest of seven suspects. Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the suspects, including a woman, are believed to be linked to the mastermind. "The suspects include three foreigners, two men and a woman.

items.title: Che' Puan Mahkota Johor: Protecting children from sexual exploitation everyone's responsibility
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Protecting children from sexual exploitation is a shared responsibility requiring close inter-agency cooperation, Che' Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Bustamam said today. The Regent of Johor's consort said children's safety and their best interests must always remain the priority. The seminar brought together agencies involved in identifying, protecting, investigating and supporting children affected by sexual exploitation.

items.title: Haze: All Johor schools to close for two days starting tomorrow by Regent’s decree over unhealthy API
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 7 — The Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail has decreed for all schools in the state to close following the persistent haze and unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings,” said Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali. He said this will be subjected to directives from the Johor Education Department (JPNJ) and relevant authorities. Dr Muhammad Naqib said the state government understands that such a decision may impact parents and guardians who still need to work.

items.title: Laos meth bust: Four arrested in Subang Airport hangar raid over 521kg found in Learjet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) today raided a hangar at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang, believed to be linked to the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs in Laos last week. Port Klang AKPS Commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said the special operation was conducted jointly with the Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (JSJN), AKPS, Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters (IPD), Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad Auxiliary Police (AVSEC) and Special Branch Travel Control Officers (TCO). The operation was conducted jointly... we had been planning it since yesterday, and the operation began at noon today and has since been completed,” he told Bernama when contacted today.

items.title: Anwar: Budget 2027 to turn economic growth into better lives for Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Fifth Madani Budget is based on a clear resolve to strengthen the nation’s economy and translate growth into a better life for the people. Anwar said he is aware that economic growth alone is insufficient if some citizens still face rising living costs. Earlier today, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, briefed the media on the Madani 2027 Budget to explain the Madani government’s direction and efforts for the people.

items.title: Johor MB pushes for Asean emergency talks as haze hits unhealthy levels
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 7 — Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi called on the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) to play a more active role and to convene an emergency meeting to address the haze crisis. He said the current transboundary haze situation is affecting Johor, particularly in the areas of public health and a deteriorating air quality in several areas of the state. Earlier today, Johor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with figures between 161 and 197, in eight monitoring stations.

items.title: Former N. Sembilan exco members barred only from exco rooms but can still enter Wisma Negeri, says A-G
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The 10 state assemblymen who previously served as Negeri Sembilan executive councillors (exco) are only barred from entering their exco rooms following their dismissal from the posts on September 24, which means they are no longer members of the state administration. The media reported today that the 10 assemblymen — Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah — who are challenging the cancellation of their appointments as state exco members, have applied to the Seremban High Court to declare their dismissals null and void, invalid and of no effect. “Decisions made while they were still exco members are valid.

items.title: Perak Perhilitan: Malayan tigers will only be captured if they threaten public safety
items.summary: Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah said the assessment takes into account the tiger’s behaviour, frequency and duration of sightings, distance from residential areas, movement patterns, and evidence of interactions or attacks involving humans or livestock. “If the assessment shows a clear and continuing threat to human safety, Perhilitan will take appropriate action based on technical assessments in the field,” he told Bernama. Pazil said tiger sightings near human settlements did not necessarily mean that their forest habitat or roaming areas were shrinking, as movements could also be influenced by prey availability, habitat conditions, human disturbance, development and land use, as well as the animals’ natural movements.

items.title: Parliament’s Palestine Caucus to submit motion on Gaza genocide for debate
items.summary: Its chairman Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the proposed motion would include calls for a lasting ceasefire, the protection of civilians, and safe, sustained and unhindered access to humanitarian aid. Syed Ibrahim, who is also Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability, said this at a press conference held in conjunction with the Three-Year Commemoration of the Gaza Genocide at the Parliament building here today. The Ledang Member of Parliament also said the motion would call for efforts to strengthen diplomatic action, including scrutiny of military assistance and arms transfers that risk facilitating violations of international law.

items.title: Haze: Education Ministry orders state and district education offices, schools to monitor haze, act based on API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has instructed state education departments (JPN), district education offices (PPD) and all educational institutions under its jurisdiction to continue monitoring the current haze situation in their respective locations to determine further action. It said the directive includes immediately suspending all outdoor activities, including outdoor gatherings and sports, particularly in areas with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings exceeding 100. “The haze situation has also resulted in several locations posting unhealthy API readings,” it said in a statement today.

items.title: Witness insists Publika office existed in Hamzah Zainudin aide’s RM350,000 corruption trial
items.summary: Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, 51, managing director of Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd (NSB), said this during cross-examination by counsel Datuk Yaacob Md Sam, appearing for Sayed Amir Muzzakkir. Yaacob: I put it to you that the handover of RM100,000 on December 4, 2020 and RM250,000 on December 16, 2020 to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir did not take place, because the said office did not exist. Wan Azhar: I disagree.

items.title: Selangor Sultan receives Silver Jubilee Keris marking 25 years on throne
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 7 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah today received the presentation of the Keris Jubli Perak, specially crafted to commemorate His Royal Highness’s 25th year on the Selangor throne. According to a post on the Selangor Royal Office Facebook page, the ceremonial keris was specially commissioned as an expression of Sultan Sharafuddin’s deep appreciation for the art, heritage and diverse traditions associated with the Malay keris . The Keris Jubli Perak is a symbolic work that chronicles Sultan Sharafuddin’s reign through the art of Malay heritage.

items.title: Perak MB tells accuser to prove allegations over special officer’s mosque speech
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 7 — Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad today said that he was unsure of the veracity of an allegation that his special officer had delivered an official speech at a mosque in Kerian, stressing that the accuser must prove the claim. Saarani said the Sultan of Perak’s decree must be obeyed and that even he, despite being the chairman of state religious affairs, would not dare to deliver a speech at any mosque. “However the person making the allegation must prove it.

items.title: Malaysia pushes to fast-track Indonesia talks on forest fire aid as haze worsens
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — Malaysia wants operational negotiations with Indonesia to be expedited to allow the country’s team to be sent to help extinguish the forest fires in that country, which have caused cross-border haze. Mohamad said he hopes that matters related to the operation can be decided quickly so that Malaysia can send a team to help their friends in Indonesia extinguish the extensive and spreading forest fires, especially in Kalimantan. Previously, the media reported that Indonesia accepted Malaysia’s offer to help extinguish the forest fires in the republic that caused prolonged haze for several weeks.

items.title: Nhaveen murder trial adjourned to tomorrow after defence seeks time over witness statements
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 7 — The High Court here today adjourned the defence proceedings of four men charged with the murder of teenager T. Nhaveen to tomorrow. The defence sought an adjournment on the ground that it required time to follow up on the delivery of four witness statements to the prosecution today. Counsel Maanveer Singh Dhillon, appearing for the four accused, informed the court that the defence had limited time to meet them in prison to prepare the said witness statements.

items.title: Sun bear still on the loose as Perhilitan widens Seremban search
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 7 — Police have stepped up patrols around Taman Tuanku Ja’afar (TTJ) after a sun bear was spotted in the residential area, with authorities widening the search as the animal remains uncaught. Negeri Sembilan Perhilitan director Wan Mat Wan Harun said the department had widened its search after the bear failed to enter a trap set nearby. Wan Mat said this was the first report the department had received of a sun bear entering the TTJ residential area.

items.title: Two senior students to face murder charge tomorrow over Kuala Pilah sports school death
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 7 — Two 16-year-old boys suspected of involvement in the death of a younger boy at a sports school in Kuala Pilah last month are expected to be charged with murder tomorrow, Berita Harian reported. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said that the investigation papers had been referred to the state prosecution office. He said the prosecution had instructed that both suspects be charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, which deals with acts done by several people with a common intention.

items.title: Two corporate figures with 'Datuk Seri’, 'Datuk Wira’ titles out on MACC bail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Two corporate figures, who are brothers holding the titles of Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira and who were previously remanded for five days to assist investigations into abuse of power and irregularities involving an investment of about RM10 million, have been released on Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) bail. According to MACC sources, the suspect with the ‘Datuk Wira’ title was released on Monday (Oct 5) after his remand period ended. “The other suspect, with the ‘Datuk Seri’ title, was released today after his remand period, which was extended by two days, ended,” the sources added.

items.title: Higher Education Ministry says institutions given autonomy to adjust learning mode when API exceeds 201
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — Higher education institutions (IPTs) in areas recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 201 have been given the flexibility to determine suitable teaching and learning (PdP) modes to reduce health risks while ensuring students’ education continues In a statement today, the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) said it was closely monitoring air quality and had directed all institutions under its purview to monitor API readings in their respective areas. Bernama reported that 35 areas recorded unhealthy API readings as of 10 am today. API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.

items.title: ‘I was both her mother and friend’: Zara Qairina’s mother tells inquest
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 7 —The mother of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir testified at the Coroner’s Court today that she was the teenager’s principal confidante, to whom her daughter confided her troubles, joys, sorrows and matters concerning her friendships. “My relationship with Zara Qairina was indeed close. Throughout Zara Qairina’s years in primary school, Noraidah testified that she had never observed her daughter suffering any serious emotional or behavioural difficulties.

items.title: Revoked excos fight back: Ten ask High Court to void Negeri Sembilan gazette
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Ten Negeri Sembilan state executive councillors (excos) have sued the state government in the High Court to challenge the revocation of their appointments, their lawyers said today. They want the court to declare that the revocation, gazetted on September 24, is invalid. The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umairah Hashim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: Air quality deteriorates as 37 stations enter unhealthy bracket, Klang Valley and Johor hard hit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated further late this afternoon, with 37 monitoring stations nationwide recording readings in the unhealthy bracket as of 4.30pm, according to Department of Environment (DoE) surveillance data. Cheras in Kuala Lumpur followed closely behind with an API reading of 187, while Nilai in Negeri Sembilan registered 185, Putrajaya posted 183, and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 180. In Selangor, six stations logged elevated pollution levels.

items.title: Seven suspects: Chinese national latest held as Pahang police close in on RM1.7m Genting jewellery heist
items.summary: The man was detained after arriving at Kuala Lumpur International Airport yesterday and has been remanded until October 10 to assist police investigations, The New Straits Times reported today. “The man has been remanded until October 10 to assist investigations. “Police have so far arrested five foreigners and two locals,” Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob was quoted as saying.

items.title: Some money in an account is linked to crime, can govt take all of it? Court of Appeal says no
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — When money from an investment scam landed in a company’s bank account, the government moved to seize everything in it, but the Court of Appeal has now drawn a line on how far such confiscation can go. A three-judge panel ruled that authorities can take money proven to be linked to a crime, but cannot automatically seize the rest of the money in the same account without evidence connecting it to the offence, news outlet Free Malaysia Today ( FMT ) reported today. The prosecution was able to trace RM360,000 directly from a bank account linked to the Comoncaps investment scam into LWC’s Hong Leong Bank account, according to the FMT report.

items.title: National Unity Ministry to study effectiveness of existing 3R, hate speech laws
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — The National Unity Ministry, through the Unity Issues Management Committee (JPIP), will undertake a comprehensive review of the effectiveness of existing legal provisions and enforcement mechanisms in addressing issues related to religion, royalty and race (3R), as well as hate speech. The committee will be co-chaired by National Unity Ministry secretary-general Datuk Haslina Abdul Hamid, Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman, Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, and Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) director-general at the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Zamri Misman. “The ministry acknowledges that various legal provisions are already in place to address issues related to 3R, hate speech and social harmony.

items.title: Azalina: Follow-up action on audits generates over RM920m in government revenue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Follow-up action on audits by the National Audit Department has contributed to revenue collection and repayments to the government amounting to RM920.91 million as at Sept 28, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said the figure demonstrated the effectiveness of audits when identified findings were followed by appropriate action. “Audit must lead to action.

items.title: Repatriation among key issues as Myanmar president arrives in Malaysia
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 7 — Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing arrived in Malaysia today for a two-day official visit, with the repatriation of Myanmar nationals in Malaysia among key issues to be discussed with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, the minister-in-attendance, was at the airport to welcome the Myanmar leader. Also present were Malaysian Government Chief Protocol Officer Datuk Rozainor Ramli and Charge d’Affaires of Malaysia to Myanmar Johan Ariff Abdul Razak.

items.title: Tax-exempt taxpayers can opt to keep using e-invoices, says Liew
items.summary: Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said they are part of the 1.1 million taxpayers among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of RM3 million or below, who are now exempt from implementing e-Invoicing. Meanwhile, Liew said companies with annual sales exceeding RM100 million began implementing e-Invoicing on Aug 1, 2024, involving 5,578 taxpayers. He said the implementation was subsequently expanded to companies with annual sales between RM25 million and RM100 million, involving 14,567 taxpayers; companies with sales between RM5 million and RM25 million, involving 51,710 taxpayers; and companies with sales between RM3 million and RM5 million, involving 25,503 taxpayers.

items.title: Melaka state election set for Nov 14 polling, Oct 31 nomination
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 7 — The Election Commission (EC) today announced November 14 for polling in the 16th Melaka state election, and set the nomination for Oct 31. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said early voting had been set for November 10 and the campaign period would run for 14 days. Regarding the Electoral Roll (DPPR) that will be used in the 16th Melaka state election (PRN), Ramlan said that a total of 687,697 voters, consisting of 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel, are eligible to vote in the state election.

items.title: Disputed Undang abandon case to depose Negeri Sembilan Yamtuan, cannot refile lawsuit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Four Undangs or traditional ruling chiefs of Negeri Sembilan — including three disputed ones — today dropped their court attempt in Kuala Lumpur to ultimately remove Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Negeri Sembilan ruler. Today, the four men — Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Datuk Muhammed Abdullah and Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin — applied to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur to withdraw their court case against the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar and the Negeri Sembilan state government. In their court case filed in July via judicial review, the four men had wanted the court to order the Menteri Besar to sign — within seven days of the court order — their April 19 declaration to “sack” Tuanku Muhriz as Negeri Sembilan ruler.

items.title: Budget 2027: Lim Guan Eng urges caution on foreign worker wage hikes over SME contract risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Federal lawmaker Lim Guan Eng (Bagan - DAP) today again called on the government to consider the financial impact on small and medium businesses amid rumours it could raise the minimum wage when tabling Budget 2027, warning that abrupt hikes could disrupt long-term commercial agreements. Lim, a former finance minister, argued that many enterprises operate under binding multi-year contracts where labor costs are fixed at agreed-upon rates. The former minister has been vocal in opposing the minimum wage hike and mandatory EPF contribution for foreign workers.

items.title: A bridge, fresh paint and ‘like Deepavali’: Wangsa Sari PPR in KL gets a makeover
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The park is just across Sungai Bonus, but for children at the Wangsa Sari People's Housing Programme here, getting there has meant balancing along water pipes. Resident Mohd Fazil Md Noor, 56, said it would also give children a safer and easier way to get to SK Wangsa Maju Section 1, where some currently walk or cycle. Wangsa Sari PPR resident Jasbee Kaur, 67, speaks to Malay Mail about the planned pedestrian bridge and the facelift.
